Given that Tom Clancy's The Division is looking to be an extremely lengthy MMO-like shooter RPG, we were wondering when review codes would be available. Ideally, we want our reviews to release at least by launch day, particularly for triple-A titles like this.

But given that The Division functions on its multiplayer servers, it doesn't come as too much of a surprise that Ubisoft has announced, through its official blog , that reviewers will have access to the game "along with everyone else when it's released on March 8." Ubisoft admits that "it's impossible for us to populate the servers in a way that would adequately replicate playing The Division on launch day."

I have mixed feelings about this - on the one hand, only giving reviewers a test version when the online component is functional arguably is not the worst of ideas, seeing how there's been some recent cases where games received positive feedback but then were canned by actual players because the online mode was virtually non-functional at launch (while it theoretically could have worked well with the much smaller number of players who got their hands of a pre-launch review version).

On the other hand, Ubisoft has become rather notorious for the severe launch bugs of its titles (we all remember Assassin's Creed Unity, now do we?), so that people who wish to buy the game immediately or want to preorder it must do so more or less blindly. Of course, this problem can easily be circumvented by not preordering the game or buying it at launch.
